title: Planning an Angular Application
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of planning an angular application and name the relevant Angular concepts.
Apply at least one syllabus item from this lesson in a focused Angular example.
Verify expected behavior and identify one compatibility, failure or trust-boundary limitation.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on planning an angular application inside Practical Application Development. Begin with the syllabus anchor “Defining requirements”, name the data or UI behavior involved, and then verify the result with a focused example. The goal is to make one clear engineering decision rather than memorize an isolated API.
content.why_it_matters: Planning an Angular Application helps keep Angular features understandable as the application grows. A small explicit pattern is easier to reuse, test and review than scattered UI-specific logic.

content_blocks.title: Mental model
content_blocks.text: **Planning an Angular Application.** This is part of **Practical Application Development**. Start from the concrete question “what changes in the application when this concept is used?” Then map the supplied syllabus terms to a small behavior, keep dependencies and trust boundaries visible, and verify what the example does. Planning an Angular Application helps keep Angular features understandable as the application grows. A small explicit pattern is easier to reuse, test and review than scattered UI-specific logic.

content.task: Apply planning an angular application to a small feature in a disposable Angular learning project. Demonstrate at least one supplied subtopic (Defining requirements), record the expected UI or console result, and include one test, failure case or version note.
task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates “Defining requirements” in the context of Planning an Angular Application.
The learner explains the expected result and includes an empty, invalid or failure case where appropriate.
Verification evidence matches the actual environment; a static CodeLeaf snippet is not described as a successfully executed Angular build.
hints: Start with the syllabus item “Defining requirements” and write down the expected behavior before changing code.
Keep the example small; include only dependencies, inputs, providers and state that the example actually needs.
Reproduce the intended behavior in a pinned local Angular workspace and inspect both normal and failure paths.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its surrounding context.
common_mistakes.why: Angular examples can depend on imports, providers, template context or a particular framework version.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the run instructions and validate against the exact generated workspace.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an attractive UI result as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Accessibility, boundary cases, failures and server-side rules may not be visible in the happy path.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a focused assertion and test at least one realistic failure state.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming client code guarantees authorization or validates all external data.
common_mistakes.why: Browser code is controlled by the client and can receive unexpected network responses.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate external values and enforce protected business rules on the backend.
